bluf: Open Influence is a Los Angeles creator marketing agency, founded in 2013 with offices from New York to London, Milan and Hong Kong, selling enterprise brands bespoke influencer programs with paid amplification and its own Studio OI production. The one current move on record is a pilot partnership in Snap's new Creator Agency Partner Program, announced in its LinkedIn ads, which points it toward platform partnerships and paid social rather than AI. A rival should know its 92% renewal claim stands on no named client, no case study found and a sitemap with 0 URLs updated in 90 days.
doing:
Open Influence positions as a Los Angeles headquartered global creator marketing agency running bespoke influencer programs end to end, from strategy and production to paid amplification. Decoded: it recruits and manages creators for large brands, produces the content in house and then pays to push the best posts as ads, each program custom built. The headline claim is a reported 92% client renewal rate, quoted as a claim; the record ties it to no client.

The sold mix leads with Creator & Influencer at score 3: the title and meta call it a global influencer marketing agency running full service creator programs since 2013. Paid Social scores 2 and is core, on paid media amplification of creator content, a Paid Social service and the Snap creator agency pilot. Content & Digital PR scores 1 with no evidence note; every other line scores 0, Data & Measurement included. The services run from Managed Services and Campaign Management to Paid Media Amplification and Omnichannel Campaign Strategies. Studio OI, its content production studio, is the one proprietary asset; the one partner is the Snap Creator Agency Partner Program, as a pilot partner.

AI posture: no AI service offer is captured; it publishes a trend report playbook on winning in AI search, and the sitemap holds 1 AI URL. AI search and AI automation score 0.

Moves: the record holds none with a date. The Snap pilot surfaces only in a LinkedIn ad: "Open Influence has been named a pilot partner in Snap Inc.'s new Creator Agency Partner Program". Pricing: the record is silent. Conspicuously absent for a creator agency selling to enterprise: case studies, named clients, a measurement line, a headcount and a named owner. Its Google ads run under the advertiser InstaBrand Inc and its Greenhouse slug reads openinfluenceinstabrand; the record does not explain that relationship.
clients:
Open Influence sells to enterprise brands from its HQ in Los Angeles and offices in San Francisco, New York, Chicago, London, Milan and Hong Kong. The record lists its verticals as alcohol and spirits, automotive, beauty and personal care, CPG, entertainment, fashion, financial, health and pharma, insurance and travel, a wide consumer spread with no account attached to any of them.

The needs read holds 0 clients. No case study, logo, press release or URL slug in the record names an account, so nothing is observed, nothing is named only and no client is shared with another tracked agency. The deepen pass found 0 case studies and 0 jobs, but it read 972 sitemap URLs and fetched 1 page, so the silence is partly the reach of the pass: absence of evidence here is not evidence of an empty book. What the silence does show is that the 92% renewal claim has no client a rival can check it against.

What the base needs, inferred from the sold mix because no client signal exists: creator programs with paid amplification for consumer brands. The Horus read places Open Influence best for KJ8 (human provenance becomes a distribution signal) through Creator & Influencer, so it is likely, low confidence, that brands in beauty, fashion and CPG ask for creator content that proves a human made it as AI labeling rules bite, which suits its lead line. It is most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) and KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two) through Paid Social; with Data & Measurement at 0, a roughly even chance these clients ask for proof of what creator spend returned before they renew.

openings:
The strongest opening is proof. Open Influence claims a 92% renewal rate while the record names 0 clients and the deepen pass found 0 case studies. A rival with named creator results in beauty, CPG, fashion or alcohol is likely, moderate confidence, to win the reference check with enterprise buyers. Falsifier: named client case studies found on openinfluence.com by a deeper fetch or the next compile.

The idle house is the second lead: 0 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and a newest dated resource from 2023-09-15, which a rival publishing weekly creator work can contrast directly. It runs paid amplification with no first party data, creative volume or measurement depth in the record (P4 partial) and Data & Measurement at 0: an offer that ties creator spend to sales is likely to undercut it with CPG and beauty buyers.

The Snap pilot deepens its bet on paid social, the line carrying its KJ6 and KJ5 exposure. Displacement at 26.7 says price is unlikely to be the way in, and with no public pricing model (P5 unknown) the comparison stays private.
